statedReasoning: Bill 146/0 (led by Věra Kovářová) amends the councilor-remuneration provisions of all three self-government statutes (obce §72/72a/72b, kraje §47/47a/47b, hl. m. Praha §53/53a/53b) in parallel. Per the full text and důvodová zpráva (now read directly from the primary cached text): the bill is a TECHNICAL FIX to zákon č. 57/2025 Sb., a March-2025 amendment (itself passed via a floor amendment) that introduced remuneration cuts for councilors who simultaneously hold another office (MP, senator, government minister, or a council seat at another territorial tier). The DZ lists five concrete drafting flaws in the 57/2025 Sb. rule: (1) wrong scope definition of which office-overlaps trigger a cut (e.g. the Prague law wrongly covers a Prague-councilor/region-councilor overlap that cannot occur in practice, while missing the real overlap between city-wide Prague council and a městská část council); (2) cuts applied even to two non-released ('neuvolněná') offices, seen as unjustifiably strict; (3) risk of double/multiple stacking cuts when 3+ offices overlap; (4) no mechanism requiring council members to notify their municipality of a qualifying overlap; (5) poor cross-referencing between the three statutes. The bill narrows the cut to overlaps involving at least one 'uvolněná' (released/full-time) office, caps the non-released-office remuneration at 0.4x of what a released councilor would get, adds a 5-day notification duty (new §72b/47b/53b), and fixes an unrelated drafting leftover on the lower/upper bound for non-released mayors' pay. Requested first-reading passage under §90(2) jednacího řádu, citing urgency because the flawed 57/2025 Sb. rule was already in force since 1 Jan 2026.
researchedContext: History confirms: distributed 25 Mar 2026 as print 146/0; government submitted a DISAPPROVING position 21 Apr 2026 (print 146/1) — the DZ text itself does not state the government's specific objection, so the substance of that disagreement remains unverified from primary text; Organizational Committee nonetheless recommended proceeding 22 Apr 2026 (Resolution 55), naming the Committee for Public Administration and Regional Development as guarantor. Census cross-check: zero undercount — the three recorded amends-edges (128/2000, 129/2000, 131/2000) match the real full-text scope exactly (confirmed directly from the fetched bill text, which touches only Čl. I/III/V of these three acts). This bill shares its lead sponsors (Kovářová, Rakušan) and an identical aggregate sponsorContractCzk figure with sibling bill tisk 24 — same underlying sponsor-tie dataset attached to two related bills, not an independent finding.

unstatedEffects.effect: The bill's subject matter is the remuneration of councilors who ALSO hold a national office (MP, senator, minister) or a second council seat — i.e. every one of the twelve sponsoring deputies falls, by definition, within the class of people whose pay this bill could affect IF any of them also currently holds a local/regional council seat. This is a structural self-referential feature common to legislators regulating rules for their own overlapping public roles. Nothing in the fetched materials confirms whether any of the twelve sponsors in fact currently holds a concurrent local or regional council mandate, so this is flagged as a disclosure-worthy structural point, not a confirmed personal-benefit finding.
unstatedEffects.whoBenefits: Undetermined — would only apply to whichever of the sponsoring MPs, if any, currently also holds a released or non-released local/regional council seat; no such concurrent mandate is confirmed in the available materials.

conflictAssessment: Lead sponsors Kovářová and Rakušan hold governance/board seats overwhelmingly in state-owned or NGO/civic entities: Kovářová sits on the supervisory board of ČEPRO, a.s. (state-owned fuel-distribution company); Rakušan chairs the supervisory board of Vodní cesty na Labi, o.p.s. (state-linked waterways body) plus several local civic bodies (a Kolín civic association, a homeowners' association, a Kutná Hora scholarship foundation). None of these entities' business — fuel distribution, inland waterways, local civic/homeowner governance — has any plausible channel into a bill about councilor-remuneration rules for concurrent-office holders. The one genuinely relevant structural point, now confirmed from the actual bill text, is noted above as an unstated effect: the bill's subject is the sponsors' own class (MPs who might also hold local office) — a disclosure-worthy structural feature of self-regulation, but not evidence of a specific personal payoff absent confirmation any sponsor holds a concurrent local mandate. No money-tie conflict found; the technical-fix framing in the DZ (correcting acknowledged drafting flaws in a March-2025 floor amendment) is specific and internally consistent, reading as genuine rather than pretextual.
